name: Idris
note: dependent types + general programming; introduced publicly as an experimental language in 2008
typeSystem: Full dependent types (types can mention values, e.g. a vector indexed by its length) combined with a Haskell-like syntax, aimed at practical general-purpose programming rather than only proof, with totality checking available on demand.
runtime: Idris 2 compiles through Chez Scheme by default, producing Scheme code, compiled support files, and an executable launcher; creating a freestanding native executable requires an additional embedding step. Earlier Idris 1 targeted C or JavaScript.

runtimes.name: Chez Scheme backend (Idris 2)
runtimes.role: Default backend: generates Chez Scheme source and compiled support files plus a launcher that runs them with Chez Scheme; tools such as chez-exe can additionally embed the runtime.

runtimes.name: Native (C backend, Idris 1)
runtimes.role: Idris 1's original backend, compiling through C.

runtimes.name: JavaScript / Node backend
runtimes.role: Compiles Idris to JavaScript for the browser or Node.js.

compilers.name: idris2
compilers.role: The Idris 2 compiler and elaborator, self-hosted in Idris.

concurrencyModel: Threads, mutexes, and typed channels are provided by libraries, but their implementation is backend-dependent; Idris 2's standard concurrency primitives are currently tied closely to the selected Scheme runtime rather than prescribing a language-wide scheduling model.

codeExample.caption: A length-indexed vector append, where the result length is tracked in the type
codeExample.source:
import Data.Vect

append : Vect n a -> Vect m a -> Vect (n + m) a
append Nil       ys = ys
append (x :: xs) ys = x :: append xs ys
